answer: I'd like to talk about the first time I spoke in front of a large audience, because it was a genuine milestone for me. A memorable first for me was trying public speaking at a fairly large event, something I had always dreaded. It happened about a year ago, when our consultancy organised a study abroad seminar for students and parents in a hall in Sirajganj. My manager asked me to give a short presentation, and my instinct was to refuse, but I forced myself to accept, partly because I knew I could not avoid it forever. In the days leading up to it, I was genuinely [[terrified]], rehearsing constantly and imagining every possible disaster. I even practised in front of my younger sister, who turned out to be a surprisingly tough audience. When the moment came, my heart was pounding and my mouth was dry. But once I started speaking, something surprising happened; I gradually became more [[composed]], and the words began to flow. By the end, I actually felt a rush of [[exhilaration]]. It was far from perfect, but I had done it, and the sense of achievement was immense. A few parents even came up afterwards with questions, which told me I had made sense. I was still shaking a little, but I was smiling from ear to ear. Honestly, pushing through that fear was genuinely [[liberating]], and it taught me that we are often far more capable than our anxiety suggests. Since then I have been much more willing to [[step outside my comfort zone]].

followUps.q: Have you given any presentations since then?
followUps.answer: Yes, several. We now hold seminars every few months, and I usually present the section on applications. I still get a few butterflies beforehand, but nothing like that first time.

followUps.q: Would you like to try any other new things in the future?
followUps.answer: I'd really like to study abroad myself one day. After helping so many students do it, I think experiencing it first-hand would be both challenging and incredibly worthwhile.

note: Set at his consultancy's study abroad seminar in Sirajganj; added audience reaction; marked 'step outside my comfort zone'.
